scope.object: Reusable procedural SKILL.md text loaded into the student context.
scope.feedback: Paired teacher/student action-observation traces; analyst identifies behavior differences and error/verification patterns. No answer labels or new environment evaluation in the default offline construction loop.
scope.retention: Sequential chunk patches persist in a final skill reused on held-out tasks.
scope.weights: No weight changes in D-Skill; SFT is a separate baseline.
scope.limit: A one-pass offline skill-transfer component, not repeated autonomous rollout-driven RSI or weight-and-Harness coevolution.

version_changes: v2 clarifies that teacher skill text never reaches the difference analyst, instead of claiming teacher skills are never visible anywhere in the pipeline.
Conclusion gap-closure range changes from 82–95% to 75–95%; Table 1 already contains 75.3% for Sonnet 5 to Haiku 4.5 chess and 94.6% maximum for ALFWorld. Tables themselves do not change.

Chess construction changes popularity threshold from at least 100 to above 70, minimum plays from 1000 to above 200, rating-deviation threshold from at most 80 to at most 85; v2 adds 50 evaluation puzzles per 400-point rating band. The explicit no-correctness-feedback sentence is removed.
Trace truncation changes from first 10000 characters plus tail within 35000 total, to first 10000 and last 35000. This is a material input-budget clarification, not just formatting.
limits: The default pipeline has no validation acceptance gate; a SkillOpt-backed ablation does retain one. Do not conflate them.
Distillation and held-out evaluation tasks are disjoint as specified, but test contamination beyond that split was not independently audited.
Three skill replicates with two passes each versus two baseline/teacher evaluation passes; not same total training cost or equal inference tokens.
SFT comparison shares teacher corpus but D-Skill also uses student traces and analyst calls.
Read methods, main tables, ablations, cost discussion, limitations, changed passages and procedural skill example; no experiment rerun or exhaustive appendix skill certification.
numeric_checks: Table 1 chess Haiku 41.2 to 52.5 versus teacher 56.2 yields 75.3% from displayed rounded means; Qwen 24.8 to 39.0 versus teacher 41.0 yields approximately 87.7%.
The v2 75–95% rounded conclusion agrees with the main-table endpoints; v1 82–95% did not include its lower chess result.
Table 1 and all HTML result table contents are unchanged between versions; pipeline construction and budget descriptions change.

evidence.quote: These lessons are consolidated into a single skill, which is loaded into the student’s context at inference time.
No stage computes a gradient or requires access to the parameters of either model.
recording the actions issued and the observations returned.
Each lesson must cite concrete evidence from the paired traces and express a task-general principle rather than an instance-specific correction.
Finally, in the apply phase, the merged patch is deterministically incorporated into the current skill before the next chunk is processed.
no correctness labels or reference solutions are supplied to the difference-analysis or skill-update stages.
The SkillOpt-backed variant retains SkillOpt’s held-out validation gate.
loading the distilled document increases inference cost relative to the bare student by adding input tokens and, in some cases, inducing additional interaction steps
Always follow a two-stage loop: inspect the entire workbook before any modification, and verify the output after saving by reloading the workbook from disk (do not rely on in-memory state).
